title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The notes study Grothendieck's 'équation des lacets'. These are the loop relations (133)(134) for a pair (ξ,η) in the profinite fundamental group Π̂_{0,3} of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, with ξ = η·l_1^ν. They are essentially the defining relations of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^ (Drinfeld's (λ,f) with λ = 2m+1). Here ν plays the role of m and μ = 2ν+1 the role of λ. On these pages Grothendieck pushes the equations into SL(2,Ẑ) through Π̂_{0,3} ≅ (profinite) Γ(2) ⊂ SL(2,Ẑ). Write ξ = [[A,B],[C,D]] and η = [[R,S],[T,U]], both ≡ 1 mod 2.

Previous page. The 2-cycle relation forces η to be symmetric, η = ᵗη, so S = T (152). The sign − is excluded by the congruence mod 2. The defining relation ξ = ε η l_1^ν, with l_1 = [[1,0],[2,1]], gives (153): ξ = ε[[R+2νS, S],[T+2νU, U]]. Comparing entries gives (154) B = εS, D = εU. A further relation (150) is linear in the entries of ξ and comes from the 3-cycle relation; it is used here in the form C − B + D = 1. Together with (154) it is equivalent to (155) μD = 1, or (155bis) μU = ε.

This page.
- Step 1. Grothendieck observes that (155), given (154) and (150), only expresses the equality of the C-entries, C = ε(T+2νU) =: C'. Check with ε = 1: C = B − D + 1 = S − U + 1 and C' = S + 2νU, and these are equal iff (2ν+1)U = 1.
- Step 2. So (154)+(155) say exactly that three of the four entries of the two sides of (153) agree: B = B', C = C', D = D'.
- Step 3. The fourth entry follows automatically. Both matrices have determinant 1, so A = (1+BC)/D and A' = (1+B'C')/D'. Since D = D' is invertible by (155), A = A'.
- Theorem. For a solution (ξ,η) ∈ Π̂_{0,3} × Π̂_{0,3} of (133)(134), take its images in SL(2,Ẑ), with the sign of η fixed by (147). Then (154) and (155) hold. Consequence (a): μ = 2ν+1 is invertible in Ẑ; it is entirely determined by ξ (μ = 1/D), but by η only up to sign (μ = ε/U).

Next page. Solutions of the projected system are shown to correspond bijectively to pairs (B,D) with B ∈ 2Ẑ and D ∈ Ẑ^*. The construction is encoded by the upper-triangular (affine/Borel) matrix u_ξ = [[1/D, B/D],[0,1]].

Purpose: to understand how much of a GT-type solution survives in the SL(2,Ẑ) (Γ(2)) quotient, and to show that the 'cyclotomic' parameter μ is forced to be a unit.
errors: On the page the second equality is written 'C = B''; by context it must be C = C'. A slip of pen or of transcription.
The marginal note on the previous page says ε = 1 under the current sign convention. ε is nevertheless carried along, harmlessly.

The next page's transcription writes (150) as 'A + D − B = 1'. The derivations there (C = B − D + 1, A = μ(1+B+B²) − B) and here (C = C' ⇔ μU = 1) only work if (150) reads C − B + D = 1. Probably a misreading or a slip, not a mathematical error.
No substantive mathematical error found. The determinant argument for A = A' is correct once D is known to be a unit.

ideas.what: Projection of the loop (GT) equations for (ξ,η), ξ = η l_1^ν, to SL(2,Ẑ) via Π̂_{0,3} ≅ Γ(2)^; entrywise comparison shows the relation reduces to B = εS, D = εU, μD = 1.
ideas.modern_name: Image of Grothendieck–Teichmüller hexagon/2-cycle relations in the congruence quotient Γ(2) ⊂ SL2(Ẑ)
ideas.usually_credited_to: GT^ itself: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; SL2-images of GT/Galois elements studied by Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps and others (exact precedence unsure)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished; Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller tower and GT idea

ideas.what: Invertibility of μ = 2ν+1 deduced from the equations themselves (μD = 1), rather than imposed as part of the definition
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (imposes invertibility in defining GT^ as the group of invertible elements of a monoid)

ideas.what: Fourth matrix entry recovered from the other three by det = 1 once D is a unit
μ determined by ξ exactly but by η only up to sign
ideas.modern_name: sign ambiguity of lifts PSL2 → SL2

missed.claim: Grothendieck derives, from the loop equations projected to SL(2,Ẑ), that the parameter μ = 2ν+1 (Drinfeld's λ = 2m+1) is automatically a unit. In the standard definitions of GT^ (Drinfeld) and of finite-level GT-shadows (Dolgushev et al.), unit-ness is usually imposed as an axiom. This page gives a short 'linear' proof that the equations force it.
missed.quote: a) μ =2ν+1 est inversible, et il est entièrement déterminé par ξ : il est déterminé par η seulement au signe près.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: In the theory of the GT monoid versus group, and of GT-shadows mod N, it matters which axioms are redundant. A quick SL2/Γ(2) argument showing λ is forced to be a unit (given the mod-2 normalisations) could simplify definitions or explain non-invertible monoid elements. Whether this is already folklore is unsure.

missed.claim: The page begins a classification of the SL(2,Ẑ)-shadows of solutions of the loop equations. It is completed on the next page as a bijection with pairs (B,D), B even, D a unit, encoded by an affine matrix u_ξ. The lifting question — which (B,D) come from genuine solutions in Π̂_{0,3}, and what the image of GT^ or G_Q in this Borel-type group is — is not addressed here.
missed.quote: On trouve ainsi le Théorème Pour une solution (ξ,η) dans Π̂_{0,3}×Π̂_{0,3} du système d'équations (133)(134)...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This relates to the image of GT^ / Galois under the Γ(2) (congruence, metabelian-type) quotient. That theme recurs in Ihara's and later work, but Grothendieck's explicit (B,D) parametrisation does not seem to be recorded.

deep.surprise_reason: The computation is elementary linear algebra. It is notable mainly as an unpublished early instance of Grothendieck working with GT-type equations (with ν exactly Drinfeld's m) projected to SL(2,Ẑ), and deducing rather than assuming that λ = 2ν+1 is a unit. Interesting historically, but a modest mathematical point.
transcription_corrections: 'B̌ = B', C = B', D = D'' should read 'B = B', C = C', D = D'' (the check mark over B is a writing artifact or correction mark).
'désignant par ξ,η [?]' — in the image these are presumably ξ̄, η̄ (images in SL(2,Ẑ)) or written in a different typeface; the reading of the symbols themselves is uncertain.
'D=D' est inversible [?]' — the reading 'inversible' is consistent with the image ('D = D' est inv., par (155)').
Header: 'des relations (154) (155) expriment le fait que les deux membres de (153) ont trois coefficients égaux, ...' — 'fait' is struck through but the sense is 'ont trois coefficients égaux'.
